clue.text: Herald for one hundred and one entering the sea in France

indicators.note: whatever enters a place ends up inside it, so these letters are planted within the ones the clue names next

parts.note: pro means in favour of — a pro-hunting vote is a vote for hunting
la mer is how the French say the sea, and it opens up in two places
a hundred is C and one is I in Roman numerals, and they go in either side of LA

explanation.walkthrough: 'In France' is the standing signal to answer in French: the clue wants the French words themselves, not an English translation of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Herald -> PROCLAIMER: a herald's job was to proclaim news aloud in the street, so the answer names the office by the announcing it does.

clue.text: Perhaps repent? Not this woman

parts.note: one thing repenting can perhaps mean is shedding — giving up what you have been
and what the penitent sheds is the evil in them

explanation.walkthrough: The enumeration is the tell: 3-5 breaks the two shed words in a place they never break in ordinary use, which is where the second reading appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Not this woman -> SHE-DEVIL: a she-devil is a woman of settled malice, so the clue names her by the repentance she is never going to manage.

clue.text: Captures one abandoning bid during sales

indicators.note: to abandon something is to walk off and leave it behind, so that letter is not in the answer at all
what happens during an event happens inside it, so these letters sit in among the others

parts.note: auctions are sales, and the word splits open after its A
a bid that has abandoned its one — I, the Roman numeral — is left as BD

explanation.walkthrough: The saleroom surface does all the work: 'bid' looks like part of the auction and is really a word waiting to be docked of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Captures -> ABDUCTIONS: both name the seizing of a person, though an abduction is the criminal kind, carrying someone off against their will.

clue.text: Hit button on the counter

indicators.note: to run counter to something is to go the opposite way, and letters sent the opposite way come out in the reverse order

parts.note: a knob is the button you push or turn, and it comes round the other way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' is the pivot the surface hides: it looks like the shop fitting the button sits on, and it is the word telling you which way to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit -> BONK: a bonk is a light knock, usually on the head, so the answer is the comic end of the general word.

clue.text: Study heart in love with love once more

parts.note: a den is the small room you shut yourself in to study

indicators.note: the heart of a word is what sits at its centre, so the outer letters are left behind and the middle is taken

parts.note: lOVe keeps these two at its centre
love is the tennis score of nothing, written as a nought

explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two different jobs a breath apart: first it is a written word with a middle, then it is a tennis score.
explanation.definitionFit: once more -> DE NOVO: the Latin tag means 'from new', and English keeps it for starting again from scratch, so it is the formal way of saying afresh.

clue.text: Perhaps Jesus and Hazard sent new losing sides

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two edges, and a word that loses them is left holding only its middle

parts.note: aNd keeps only its middle letter
hAZARd gives up the H and D at its edges
sENt is what is left once the S and T have gone
nEw keeps only its middle letter

explanation.walkthrough: Eden Hazard was a footballer, which is the transfer story the surface is selling — and even the little word 'and' is material here, not grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps Jesus -> NAZARENE: a Nazarene is anyone from Nazareth, and Jesus is the famous one, so 'perhaps' flags a definition by example.

clue.text: Upcoming artist mostly past his prime

indicators.note: a down entry runs from the top, so anything coming up it is being read from the bottom end first
mostly means nearly all of it, so the word arrives with its final letter missing

parts.note: Degas is the crossword's stock painter, and mostly he turns up without his S

explanation.walkthrough: 'Upcoming' is doing two jobs at once: it sounds like a career on the rise and it is the instruction that sends the letters up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: past his prime -> AGED: someone aged is well beyond his best years, so the phrase and the word name the same decline, one by picture and one by label.

clue.text: Unpleasant smell leaves area of city

indicators.note: something that leaves has gone out of the door, so those letters walk off and are not in the answer

parts.note: a borough is an administrative area of a city
BO is body odour, and it is the smell that walks out of the front of the word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Area of city' looks like the definition and is really the word being cut down; the definition is the lone adjective at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasant -> ROUGH: a rough night or a rough deal is a nasty one, so the answer is the everyday word for something you would rather not have had.

clue.text: One attacks occasionally dumb loyalty

indicators.note: what is done occasionally happens now and then rather than throughout, so you pick up every other letter and skip the rest

parts.note: dUmB lOyAlTy hands over its second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.walkthrough: The 1-4 enumeration is the way in: a single letter and then a word almost always means a letter-plus-noun name, and the hyphen falls inside the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: One attacks -> U-BOAT: the German submarine of both wars existed to torpedo shipping, so the definition names it by the one thing it did.

clue.text: "I hate this dessert," said one coming back

parts.note: a boo is what you shout at something you hate

indicators.note: said points at the ear rather than the page, so what counts is how the word sounds and not how it is spelt

parts.note: the dessert is a meringue, and a meringue said aloud comes out with none of its own spelling

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks sell a diner complaining about pudding, but 'said' is not reporting the speech — it is the flag that only the sound of the sweet matters.
explanation.definitionFit: one coming back -> BOOMERANG: the thrown stick that returns to the hand, so the definition picks it out by the single property everybody knows it for.

clue.text: Criminal could undo a lock without key in ideal world

indicators.note: a criminal is someone who will not keep to the rules, and letters keeping to no rules will not stay in the order they were given
in its older sense without means outside rather than lacking, so this letter stands outside the jumble instead of joining it

parts.note: a key in music is named by a letter, and C is the plainest of them
those fourteen letters come out in a completely new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the joint the surface hides: read as lacking it makes a burglary story, and read as outside it parks a single letter in front of everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: ideal world -> CLOUD-CUCKOO-LAND: the birds' city in Aristophanes, borrowed by English for any scheme too perfect to be real, so calling a plan this calls it fantasy.

clue.text: Sparks when Romeo meets Juliet set back by sides in Verona

indicators.note: letters told to go back run the other way, and in an across entry the other way is right to left

parts.note: the two of them meet in Act I of the play

indicators.note: the sides of a word are the letters at either end of it, so the middle is dropped and only the edges are kept

parts.note: Verona is left with the V and A at its two ends
the stage set, written the other way round

explanation.walkthrough: Romeo and Juliet are the NATO alphabet's R and J on any other day; here they are the lovers themselves, and what you need is the act they meet in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparks -> ACTIVATES: to spark something off is to set it going, which is exactly what activating a device does, so the two verbs swap in that sense.

clue.text: He's as burnt at sea as others in his position

indicators.note: to be at sea is to be hopelessly muddled, and muddled letters have lost track of the order they came in

parts.note: the ten letters of HE'S AS BURNT come round again in a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' is not a place in this clue but a state of confusion — and the beach it conjures up is exactly where the surface wants your eye to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: others in his position -> SUNBATHERS: everyone else stretched out on the sand doing what he is doing, so the definition names the group by the pose they share.

clue.text: I've finished speaking special spell

definitions.note: A spell is one stretch of bowling and the answer is plural: the setter defines the units by the single passage of play they add up to.

parts.note: 'over' is what a radio operator says to hand the conversation back
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.walkthrough: Over as a radio sign-off and over as a cricketing unit are the two halves of the joke, and the clue plays one against the other.
explanation.definitionFit: spell -> OVERS: a bowler's spell at the crease is measured out in overs, so the cricketing sense ties a passage of play to its six-ball units.

clue.text: How to make waxing glide and move smoothly

definitions.meaning: Read straight, this is a question about polish: floors and skis are waxed precisely so that things slip along them
The setter means smooth in the other sense — the sly move of a charmer, made while the two of you are gliding round the floor

explanation.walkthrough: There is no wordplay to separate out here: the whole sentence is the joke, and 'waxing' is what does the misleading, being the beauty treatment rather than the polish.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue is one wry question, and its answer is the classic smooth move — a kiss taken on the quiet is what keeps a romance gliding.

clue.text: Where you might find husband off the beaten track

parts.note: H is the crossword's standing abbreviation for husband
this asks a question, and the answer is the reply to it: it says whereabouts in a word that letter is sitting

explanation.walkthrough: NOWHERE has seven letters with the H dead centre, so the answer is its own address — it tells you where the husband is by describing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: off the beaten track -> MIDDLE OF NOWHERE: both phrases mean far from anywhere anyone goes, one by naming the missing road and the other the emptiness around it.

clue.text: United go over stopping time to attack — it's not going to work

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to fill it, so these letters are pushed into the middle of the ones already there

parts.note: D-Day was the appointed hour for the invasion, and the word splits after its D
U is the abbreviation United takes in a club's name
to vet a plan is to go over it carefully

explanation.walkthrough: D-Day is the piece to spot: 'time to attack' is a date in 1944 before it is anything else, and the football club is there to keep you on a pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: not going to work -> DUVET DAY: the informal name for a day spent in bed rather than at the office, so the answer nicknames the absence.

clue.text: Time to stick spring chicken in that case

indicators.note: to stick something somewhere is to shove it in, so this letter goes inside the piece it is shoved into

parts.note: a spring rising in the ground is a well
a hen is the chicken in the yard, and she opens up to take the T
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring chicken' is the trap: as a phrase it means a youngster, and the clue wants its two words prised apart and read one at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: in that case -> WELL THEN: both are what you say to move a conversation along once a condition has been granted, so they swap over in speech.

clue.text: Show regret overtaking Tesla, say

indicators.note: a car overtaking passes right around the one in front, so these letters end up with the others on both sides of them

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it, and RUE splits after its R
a Tesla is one make of EV, the electric vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface is a stretch of road — overtaking, a Tesla — and the only word not driving anywhere is the one-word definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Show -> REVUE: a revue is a stage entertainment of sketches and songs, so the general word for the evening clues one particular form of it.

clue.text: Attention-seeking academic's plea to retire — it makes you sick

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw the way you came, so the letters are read back along the line they arrived on

parts.note: an academic hungry for attention begs to be quoted in your footnotes: cite me

explanation.walkthrough: The plea is a real sentence spoken by a real academic, which is the whole joke — nothing has to be done to it except read it the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: it makes you sick -> EMETIC: an emetic is a medicine given to bring on vomiting, so the definition is its entire purpose rather than a side effect.

clue.text: Post from sketch show entertaining great man in audience

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside the house, so these letters are taken in by the ones around them

parts.note: Saturday Night Live, the sketch show known by its initials, and it opens up before its L
A1 means top quality, and its 1 is written as the Roman numeral

indicators.note: an audience gets the sound of a word and never its spelling, so you write down what you would hear

parts.note: a man is a male, and a male said out loud is spelt the postal way

explanation.walkthrough: A1 for 'great' is the piece worth banking: the numeral turns into a Roman I, which is how two letters come out of a one-syllable word.
explanation.definitionFit: Post -> SNAIL MAIL: the joking name email gave to letters carried by hand, so the answer is the post named for how slow it looks beside a screen.

clue.text: I taxi over after heading to Ann Summers

indicators.note: something turned over comes out the other way up, so those letters are read in the opposite order
the heading stands at the top of a piece of writing, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Ann
a taxi is a cab, and it turns round
the clue's own I, taken at face value

explanation.walkthrough: Ann Summers is a high-street lingerie chain, and that is the whole of the misdirection: the name has to come apart into one letter and a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Summers -> ABACI: an abacus is a machine for summing, so 'summers' names the beads-and-wire adders by the job they do, in the Latin plural.

clue.text: Set for success from section of record following where Trump lies

indicators.note: to follow is to come along behind, so this piece takes its place after the one the clue goes on to name

parts.note: a politician of that stripe lies on the right of the spectrum
each separate song on a record is a track

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lies' is the pivot: the surface offers a politician telling untruths, and the wordplay wants only the direction in which he is lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Set for success -> ON THE RIGHT TRACK: the idiom says you are headed the way that gets you there, so it promises an outcome rather than reporting one.

clue.text: Some sexy group needing erection

indicators.note: some of a thing is a part of it and not the whole, so the letters are already sitting there waiting to be lifted out
to erect something is to stand it up, and standing letters up in a down entry means reading them from the bottom

parts.note: the run of letters in sexY GROup climbs the entry and hands them over the other way round

explanation.walkthrough: Every word is doing two jobs at once: as English the sentence describes the answer, as instructions it points at four letters lying face down in the middle of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight as its own definition: what is described is exactly a sexy group, and the erection it needs is the joke the letters are hiding under.

clue.text: Dirtbag occasionally pens love letter

indicators.note: what happens occasionally happens now and then, so you take every other letter and leave the ones between
to pen an animal is to shut it in, so this letter is kept inside the others

parts.note: dIrTbAg hands over its second, fourth and sixth letters
love is the nothing of a tennis score, written as a nought

explanation.walkthrough: 'Love letter' is the phrase the surface builds and the clue immediately splits: one of those words is a nought and the other is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: letter -> IOTA: the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, so the plain word names it by its class — and it is the iota of 'not one iota'.

clue.text: Fighter happy a riot erupted

indicators.note: an eruption throws everything up in the air, and what is thrown up in the air comes down in a different arrangement

parts.note: glad is the plain synonym, and it goes in unshuffled
the five letters of A RIOT come out in a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'A riot' does double duty in the surface — the scene of chaos in the story, and five letters to be rearranged in the clue — while only the first word is definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighter -> GLADIATOR: the armed man who fought for the crowd in a Roman arena, so the general word is being answered with one historical kind of it.

clue.text: Team appearing in French and Saunders finally retires

indicators.note: to appear in something is to turn up inside it, so these letters end up within the ones beside them

parts.note: et is the French for and, and it splits to take the team
a side of eleven is written XI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: finally points at the end of the run, so only the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the last letter of Saunders

explanation.walkthrough: French and Saunders are a comedy double act, and the clue splits them down the middle: one name supplies a French word, the other only its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: retires -> EXITS: retire in its stage sense means to withdraw and leave the scene, which is what an exit is — not the pension sense the surface offers.
